newsitem.title: USA: U.S. out of global family planning programs - report.
newsitem.headline: U.S. out of global family planning programs - report.

text.p: The United States, under pressure from anti-abortion groups, has backed away from its commitment to international family planning and population programmes, a Rockefeller Foundation report said on Tuesday.

The United States contributed $546 million to such programmes two years ago, but Congress last year cut funding by 35 percent and no money will be spent until July 1 unless Congress approves a resolution in February.

The report, entitled "High Stakes: the United States, Global Population and Our Common Future," decries the loss of U.S. leadership in providing contraception and other basic health services to developing countries.
In 1995, the United States provided at least 40 percent of the total $1 billion in aid from industrialised countries for population programmes. Japan, at 10 percent, was the next biggest donor.

"I'm convinced that U.S. support of international family planning has been an investment with enormous return in the realisation of human potential," said David Rockefeller, grandson of the foundation's founder, in a letter introducing the report.

The report noted that the United Nations has estimated that family planning programmes have helped curb population growth and that by the year 2050 there would be about 500 million fewer people in the world than previously estimated.

The report also disputed the idea that family planning programmes lead to an increase in abortions. It cited evidence that the abortion rate in Hungary fell sharply because of programmes promoting contraception.
